cycle.dedupe_against: EVERY finding seen this node, not only confirmed ones
cycle.why: final bug sweep is unknown-size discovery; a counter would miss the tail

forbidden: any source file - verification checks NEVER write code

verification.why: Gates are the implementer grading its own homework. A verifier is a separate agent with FRESH CONTEXT whose only job is to kill the work.
verification.evidence: Google Research: independent agents amplify errors 17.2x; a centralised orchestrator as validation bottleneck reduces it to 4.3x.
verification.no_fanout_on_implementation: Same research: multi-agent on sequential reasoning tasks scores -70%. Implementation stays single-agent.

human_gates.gate: Firestore rules and public read go live
human_gates.why: public read is hard to un-publish; confirm every record is synthetic first
this is the submission's live link; once shared it is judged

human_gates.gate: APK published on the landing page
human_gates.why: an installed APK cannot be recalled from a judge's phone

architecture.principle: Fan out only genuinely decomposable work. Sequential reasoning stays single-agent.
evidence: Google Research: sequential reasoning tasks score -70% across every multi-agent variant
graph-engineering repo stop rule: parallel configurations win ~80%, sequential work loses across configurations
Google Research: error amplification 17.2x independent vs 4.3x with a centralised orchestrator

shapes.serial: one agent, bounded subgraph, no fan-out
shapes.diamond: split -> N parallel workers with contracts -> merge in code
shapes.diamond+cycle: diamond, then loop-until-dry until 2 consecutive empty rounds

architecture.verifier_note: Every node now gets at least a spec skeptic. Fan-out is native, so breadth is affordable; the -70% finding constrains implementation, not verification.

isolation.reason: A collision means the node contract was drawn wrong. Every worker now owns a disjoint set of paths plus its own manifest; the merge is plain code that assembles the shared files. There is nothing left to collide.
isolation.roadmap_alignment: Step 3: bounded input, bounded output, exactly one job. Step 4: the reduce is plain code and edges are free. Step 10 says worktrees are the seatbelt for the one topology that needs it, not a default tax.
isolation.cost_avoided: 14 full Android checkouts for T1.3, and one merge becoming fourteen.
isolation.when_worktrees_WOULD_be_right: If a future diamond's workers must each modify the SAME existing file - a cross-cutting refactor, a rename across call sites. We have no such node. If one is ever added, isolate it; do not widen the contracts to fit.
isolation.workers_never_commit: Only the parent commits, once, after the merge. Avoids git index contention entirely.
isolation.guard: python3 scripts/fanout_check.py <node> - asserts no worker wrote outside its owned paths and no two workers claimed the same path.

always_read.rule: Re-read these at the START of EVERY node, in addition to the node's `reads` array. The DROP step discards node context, which would otherwise drop the contract itself. These four are small and they are what stop scope drift across a long run.
